card.statement:
A symplectic resolution $(X,\omega)$ is conical if there exists a $\mathbb{Z}$ -grading on the coordinate ring $\mathcal{O}(X)$ such that

•

The grading $\mathcal{O}(X)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathcal{O}(X)^{n}$ is non-negative, with $\mathcal{O}(X)^{0}=k$ and $\mathcal{O}(X)^{1}=0$.

•

The Poisson bracket has degree $-2$.

We refer to this $\mathbb{Z}$ -grading as the conical grading.

Note that the Poisson bracket is $(-2)$ -shifted with respect to the conical grading, and hence $\mathcal{O}(X)^{2}$ forms a Lie algebra with respect to the Poisson bracket.
card.label: Definition 2.4

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
